lesson.intro: La pasiva cambia el foco: el objeto de la accion pasa a ser el sujeto de la frase. Se usa cuando el que hace la accion es desconocido, evidente o poco importante, o cuando quieres sonar impersonal (textos formales, cientificos, noticias). La formula no cambia nunca: be (en el tiempo que toque) + participio pasado.

sections.heading: 1 - Voz pasiva: cuando se usa
sections.body:
Elige la pasiva cuando:

  • el agente es desconocido (My bike was stolen), evidente (The thief was arrested) o irrelevante.
  • quieres poner el foco en quien o que recibe la accion.
  • buscas un tono impersonal / formal (informes, ciencia, prensa).

Estructura: be + participio pasado.
examples: My bike was stolen.
English is spoken here.
The bridge was built in 1890.
Mistakes were made.

sections.heading: 2 - Pasiva en presente
sections.body:
• Present simple: am / is / are + participio → Rice is grown in Asia.
  • Present continuous: am / is / are being + participio → The road is being repaired right now.

Negativa: isn't / aren't (being) + participio. Pregunta: Is / Are + sujeto + (being) + participio.
examples: These rooms are cleaned every day.
Millions of emails are sent every second.
The house is being painted at the moment.
Where are these shoes made?

sections.heading: 3 - Pasiva en pasado
sections.body:
• Past simple: was / were + participio → The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo.
  • Past continuous: was / were being + participio → The room was being cleaned when I arrived.
examples: The windows were cleaned yesterday.
This castle was built in the 12th century.
Was the package delivered on time?
The stadium was being built when the storm hit.

sections.heading: 4 - Pasiva en perfect y futuro
sections.body:
• Present perfect: has / have been + participio → The project has been finished.
  • Futuro con will: will be + participio → The winners will be announced.
  • going to: is/are going to be + participio.
  • Future perfect: will have been + participio.
examples: The parcel hasn't been delivered yet.
All flights have been cancelled.
Your order will be shipped tomorrow.
A new bridge is going to be built here.

sections.heading: 5 - Pasiva con modales
sections.body:
modal + be + participio: must be done, can be seen, should be taken, has to be sent, might be delayed.

Negativa: modal + not + be + participio (This switch must not be touched).
examples: This form must be completed in black ink.
Nothing can be done until tomorrow.
The homework should be handed in by Friday.
Seatbelts must be worn at all times.

sections.heading: 6 - El agente con 'by'
sections.body:
Anade by + agente solo cuando aporta informacion util o inesperada (written by Shakespeare, discovered by Fleming).

Omite el agente si es desconocido, evidente (the thief was arrested [by the police]) o "la gente en general".

Para el instrumento se usa with, no by: broken with a hammer.
examples: Hamlet was written by Shakespeare.
The town was destroyed by the earthquake.
This house was built in 1900. (agente omitido)
The window was broken with a stone.

sections.heading: 7 - Transformar activa en pasiva
sections.body:
Tres pasos:

  1. El objeto de la activa pasa a ser el sujeto de la pasiva.
  2. El verbo se pone en be + participio, en el mismo tiempo que tenia la activa.
  3. El sujeto de la activa se vuelve by + agente (opcional).

Verbos con dos objetos (give, send, offer, tell): cualquiera puede ser el sujeto → Ana was given a prize / A prize was given to Ana.
examples: They sell tickets online. → Tickets are sold online.
Someone has taken my seat. → My seat has been taken.
They will paint the house. → The house will be painted.
The teacher gave Ana a prize. → Ana was given a prize.

sections.heading: 8 - Elegir activa o pasiva; errores
sections.body:
Usa la activa cuando el agente es conocido y relevante: es mas directa y clara. No abuses de la pasiva: hace el texto vago y pesado.

Los verbos intransitivos (arrive, happen, fall, come, go, exist...) no tienen pasiva.

En ingles informal se usa get en vez de be: He got fired.
examples: The accident happened yesterday. (no 'was happened')
My phone got stolen at the party. (informal)
The mixture was heated to 90 °C. (informe de laboratorio)

mistakes: NO: The house was build in 1900. -> SI: The house was built in 1900.
NO: A decision will made soon. -> SI: A decision will be made soon.
NO: This form must completed. -> SI: This form must be completed.
NO: The accident was happened. -> SI: The accident happened. (verbo intransitivo)
NO: The road is repairing right now. -> SI: The road is being repaired right now.
NO: The window was broken by a hammer. -> SI: ... broken with a hammer.
NO: My seat has taken. -> SI: My seat has been taken.
